gloss: stirring; slight movement of the body

definitions.gloss: stirring; slight movement of the body; fidgeting
definitions.explanation: A small, often unconscious movement of the body, such as shifting one's weight, squirming, or fidgeting. Most commonly used in the negative — 身じろぎもしない or 身じろぎもせず — to describe someone remaining perfectly still.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}は{身|み}じろぎもせずに{獲物|えもの}を{見|み}つめていた。
examples.english: The cat watched its prey without stirring at all.

examples.japanese: {緊張|きんちょう}のあまり、{身|み}じろぎ{一|ひと}つできなかった。
examples.english: I was so nervous that I couldn't move a muscle.

notes:
A literary and descriptive word almost always encountered in negative constructions. The pattern {身|み}じろぎもしない (not stirring at all) is a common literary device to convey tension, concentration, or fear.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {身|み}じろぎもしない: not moving at all; perfectly still
- {身|み}じろぎもせず: without stirring (connective form)
- {身|み}じろぎ{一|ひと}つしない: not making the slightest movement

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {微動|びどう}だにしない: not budging an inch — very similar in meaning and usage
- じっとする: to stay still; to keep motionless — more everyday
- {動|うご}かない: not moving — plain, neutral description

ETYMOLOGY:
From {身|み} (body) and じろぐ (to stir, to shift), an older verb meaning to move slightly. The verb じろぐ itself is rarely used independently in modern Japanese.

forms.negative: {身|み}じろぎしていなかった
